chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Qasim ibn al-Fuzayl, from Rabi'i, from al-Fuzayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Concerning the man who is appointed as executor of a will, he said: 'If it (the appointment) was sent to him from a city, then it is not permissible for him to reject it.'

key_terms.بَلَد: city/town — implying distance and formal dispatch of the appointment
key_terms.بُعِثَ بِهَا: it was sent/dispatched — referring to the formal communication of the appointment
key_terms.رَدُّهَا: to reject/refuse it — declining the appointment as executor
key_terms.يُوصَى إِلَيْهِ: the one appointed as executor of a will (al-wasi) — a legal guardian entrusted with carrying out the deceased's final wishes

ai.seo_question: Can an executor reject a will assignment that was sent to them from another city in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a specific jurisprudential question: when a person is appointed as executor (wasi) of someone else's will and the appointment document is formally dispatched to them, they are legally obligated to accept. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that once the notification of appointment has been formally sent from one city to the appointee, the executor cannot simply refuse the responsibility. This ruling reflects the principle in Islamic law that a trusteeship (wilaya) accepted or formally assigned carries binding obligations, particularly when the testator may have already died or is unable to designate another.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Qasim Bin Al Fuzayl, from Rabie, from Al Fuzayl, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said regarding the man whose appointment as an executor was sent to him: ‘If it was sent to him from within the city, so it is not upon to him to reject it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl from Rib’iy from al-Fudayl

who has narrated the following: “About the case of a man who is appointed as the executor of the will abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, has said, ‘If the appointment is sent from one town to another town he cannot refuse to accept the appointment.’”
